Subject: Post-cutover: frequent timeouts to inference endpoints

Hi Laura / Redwood team,

We completed the staged cutover for private connectivity to the Redwood cluster at 15:00 (our side) and immediately started seeing intermittent request timeouts and 502s for the inference endpoints. Symptoms: about ~10-15% of requests fail with connection reset / timeout, some TCP connections hang for >30s. Attached is a traceroute from one of our app hosts and a sample curl showing the timeout.

We tested from multiple on-prem hosts and see the same pattern. No configuration changes on our side except the cutover. Can you escalate on your side? This is impacting a small percentage of production traffic but spikes during larger requests.

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Collected tcpdump on the east-edge egress interface for flows to 10.2.18.0/24. See attached pcap stub (tcpdump_edge_syn-20270824.pcap).
- Observed a high number of SYN retries and duplicate SYNs where client SYNs go out but SYN-ACKs arrive on a different path and get dropped locally due to conntrack/state mismatch. That looks like asymmetric routing + SNAT collision.
- BGP snapshot: nothing obvious in terms of flaps in the immediate window; I attached bgp_adj_snapshot-20270824.txt (local RIB + adj info).

Key findings:
1) On our edge we currently have a default SNAT policy that NATs internal worker egress to a small pool (100.65.200.0/28). The customer side is also applying SNAT on their egress (on-prem NAT) and they have overlapping ephemeral ranges causing return traffic to go back to the wrong device in our NAT table. This can cause asymmetric flows and SYN retries.
2) PMTU hints: a subset of flows show DF=1 with MSS 1460 and a downstream MTU of ~1424 reported in trace, causing fragmentation failures for larger payloads. No automatic PMTU discovery fallback was observed in the traces.

Immediate mitigations to propose:
- Temporary: add explicit SNAT exclusion for the customer's source subnets (10.2.0.0/16) at the edge so we do not rewrite those flows. That should remove SNAT collisions and eliminate asymmetric path-dependent state.
- Apply MSS clamping on the edge egress for that peer to 1360 to avoid fragmentation for tunneled paths.

Ask for NetScale PS: can you confirm whether any edge policy changed at 15:00 and whether you can push a temporary MSS clamp and SNAT exception on the transit edge? If not, we'll push from our side but want alignment.

I'll keep digging into conntrack counters and will post exact iptables rules to add.

-rishi
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Post-cutover: frequent timeouts to inference endpoints

Hi all — we pulled edge telemetry and config around the event window. Summary: no control-plane BGP flaps were recorded at 15:00; however, we did have a planned micro-config change to an MPLS tagging policy on the transit pair at 14:55 that reduced available path MTU by ~32 bytes for tunneled traffic on one intermediate hop. That aligns with the MTU/fragmentation symptoms.

Actions we've taken from the PS side: 
- Pushed a temporary MSS clamp of 1360 on the egress toward the Acme peer on the transit edge.
- Confirmed that MPLS tag handling has been reverted to pre-cutover behavior to restore path MTU.
- Created a temporary route-map to prefer the non-tunneled path for 10.2.18.0/24 while we validate.

We also observed the SNAT overlap Rishi called out: the customer's on-prem NAT pool partially overlapped with our ephemeral SNAT pool. We can coordinate and carve a /28 exception on the edge to stop NAT for that prefix — but we recommend Redwood apply the exception inside your SNAT policy so customer-originated flows are preserved end-to-end.

Attached logs: bgp_adj_snapshot-20270824.txt (local view) and a pcap extract showing SYN / SYN-ACK arriving on different egresses.

NetScale PS
ps@netscale.ai

Team / Elizabeth — final update for the morning:

What we changed (completed 08:45 PT):
- Redwood applied an explicit SNAT exclusion for Acme prefixes (10.2.0.0/16) on the east-edge NAT policy. This prevents Redwood NAT translation for traffic originated by the customer and removes conntrack asymmetry.
- NetScale confirmed the temporary MSS clamp (1360) and reverted the MPLS tagging change that reduced MTU.
- We updated the runbook (link below) to add a pre-cutover checklist: verify SNAT pools do not overlap, confirm MSS clamp policy for tunneled paths, and run a PMTU test.

Current customer status: Elizabeth reports no timeouts in the last 90 minutes from their test harness and successful synthetic load tests. We'll leave the temporary route-map in place for 24 hours and monitor.

Postmortem ask / follow-ups:
- Operations: convert the temporary SNAT exception to a documented, auditable exception with an expiration + owner.
- Net: validate path MTU end-to-end and add a monitoring alert for PMTU changes on transit.
- SRE: add a quick health-check to the canary that validates 3-way handshake success rate per-minute (failures >1% -> rollback).

Thanks for the fast triage everyone. Elizabeth — can you confirm you’re happy to close the incident if you see no regressions in the next 24h? We’ll follow up with a short postmortem doc.

Best,
Laura Bennett
